rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A: verify dividend trajectory via 10-K cash-flow + Q1 2026 10-Q dividends paid line; Mode-B: quantify the cut as % of prior rate and link to debt-service / margin-call narrative.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Annual dividends paid: 2023 $181.7M, 2024 $189.4M, 2025 $150.1M (already declining). Q1 2026 dividends paid per 10-Q cash-flow statement = $1.30M vs $49.13M Q1 2025 — a 97.4% decline. Implied per-share quarterly dividend dropped from ~$0.985 to $0.02 (-98%). The 10-K frames this as 'careful monitoring of liquidity and cash requirements' but the cut coincides with: (a) $750M 7% 2027 Notes maturing in 13 months from the 10-K filing date, (b) FY2025 net cash provided by operating activities of NEGATIVE $10.6M (vs -$8.6M 2024, +$17.3M 2023), and (c) the CEO's August 2025 margin-call forced liquidation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cogent had been a dividend-growth telecom story for 13 years. A 98% dividend cut, executed Q4 2025 and ratified for Q1/Q2 2026, with the issuer's own explanation citing 'lingering impact of bank failures' rather than the obvious 2027 refinancing wall, is a major commitment-narrative break. Mode-B: the cut frees only ~$190M of annual cash — meaningful but insufficient against $750M of 2027 maturities — yet management chose to cut by 98% rather than a more moderate amount, signaling either deep concern about refinancing pricing or covenant-protective behavior.

rfm_tuples.R: (Implicit Mode-B claim: management commitment in an extreme drawdown should manifest as open-market code-P purchases, NOT forced lender liquidations.)

rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO Dave Schaeffer (Chairman/CEO/President) Form 4 footnotes for Aug 7 2025: 'The sales reported on this Form 4 represent a non-volitional transfer of Common Stock by the Reporting Person to one of the Reporting Person's lenders effectuated by the lender pursuant to the Reporting Person's margin loan facility. The lender then sold the Common Stock to one of its affiliates at a 7% discount to the then market price.' Aug 8 2025 footnote nearly identical, lender block-sold at 9% discount. Schaeffer's two-day liquidation: 1,840,669 shares @ $32.60 ($60.0M) + 818,909 shares @ $27.50 ($22.5M) = 2,659,578 shares for $82.5M proceeds going to the lender, not to Schaeffer. No prior public disclosure of the pledge in the 10-K Item 12 / proxy 'pledged securities' table was uncovered in this review (only the policy disclosure exists). The CEO Form 4 sales totals: 2024 = 12 tx / 505,000 sh / $33.5M / avg $66.37; 2025 = 38 tx / 3,758,578 sh / $136.6M / avg $36.35. 2024-2025 lifetime total: $170.1M in proceeds. No CEO sales in 2026 pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the dispositive finding. The CEO had pledged a substantial share position (≥2.66M shares) as margin loan collateral. When the stock fell through the pledge threshold in August 2025, his lender force-liquidated 5%+ of his position over two days. Force liquidations at 7-9% discounts to market are themselves price-depressing events and signal the borrower had no remaining liquidity to top up margin. For a founder/CEO of a 'mature, dividend-paying' telecom to have this much leverage outstanding against his own stock is itself a major commitment-narrative break that the Insider Trading Compliance Policy (10-K Item 10, Exhibit 19.1) appears not to have prohibited. There is ZERO offsetting code-P open-market purchase by Schaeffer (or any officer) in 2025-2026 despite a -64.6% drawdown.

rfm_tuples.R: (Implicit Mode-B: if the drawdown is overdone and management views the business as durable, the canonical commitment signal would be code-P open-market purchases by C-suite/directors into weakness.)

rfm_tuples.M_value: Only 3 code-P purchases in the entire pre-cutoff Form 4 window since 2023: Director Marc Montagner — 2022-11-09 (5,000 sh @ $54.85) + 2022-11-09 (5,000 sh @ $54.90) + 2024-06-11 (10,000 sh @ $52.61). Total purchase activity ever: 20,000 shares / $1.07M. NO purchases by Director Montagner (or any other director/officer) AFTER the August 2025 margin-call event when stock collapsed below $30, and none during the entire 2025-2026 drawdown window. Sell:Buy ratio at C-suite level since 2023 is functionally infinite ($191M sold by CEO Schaeffer vs $0 officer purchases).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Zero C-suite open-market purchases into a -64.6% drawdown, against $191M of CEO sales (much of it forced) in the prior 24 months, fails the Form-4 commitment test. Even Director Montagner — who has historically been the buyer in past dislocations (2022, 2024) — did not buy in 2025-2026. The absence of buying by the one director who has reliably bought every prior dip is a discriminating Mode-B finding.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B: quantify refinancing exposure vs available liquidity, capital-allocation choices, and external rate environment.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Maturity schedule (10-K Note 4): 2026 $0, 2027 $750.0M, 2028 $0, 2029 $206.0M, 2030 $174.4M, Thereafter $600.0M; total long-term debt at par $1.73B + $623.4M finance leases = $2.4B. Cash + restricted cash Dec 31 2025 = $205.1M (restricted $56.6M; unrestricted ≈ $148.5M). FY2025 operating cash flow NEGATIVE $10.6M. The $750M 2027 Notes carry a 7.00% coupon — they were issued in June 2022 and 2024 when spreads were materially tighter; refinancing 2027 at June-2025-style terms cost the company a 6.50% secured coupon on the 2032 Notes WITH the addition of secured collateral. Refinancing the 2027 unsecured stack on similar terms would likely require either (a) secured collateral, raising structural-subordination concerns for the existing 2032 secured noteholders, (b) equity issuance into a distressed stock, or (c) materially higher cash interest.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 2027 refinancing problem is the implicit driver of the dividend cut, the August margin-call cascade, and the Form-4 evidence. The 10-K acknowledges refinancing risk in generic risk-factor language but does NOT quantify the cash gap. With unrestricted cash of ~$148M, negative operating cash flow, and $750M due in 16 months from the 10-K filing date, the maturity wall is the central distress driver. Management's chosen capital-allocation path — preserve dividend at $0.02 token level + buy back stock under the $105.8M remaining authorization rather than de-lever aggressively — suggests insufficient runway to maintain even modest investor optics.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Three SPE landlords all owned by CEO Schaeffer: Sodium LLC (HQ; $1M/yr fixed since 2015), Thorium LLC (54,803 sf office space), Germanium LLC (additional space). Disclosure says these were Board-approved; no third-party fair-market comparables disclosed in the 10-K. Combined with the August 2025 margin-loan forced liquidation, the structural picture is: CEO is simultaneously (a) reporting-person seller of $191M of stock; (b) landlord receiving recurring rental income; (c) recipient of new performance-based equity awards in 2026 with $70/$85/$100 price targets — i.e., asymmetric upside in a recovery while the cash payments flow regardless. None of these are inherently improper, but the combination is a governance-quality flag.

Mode-B is the concerning angle: in a distressed/refinancing scenario, the CEO collects rent on three properties via private entities AND was recently granted re-priced performance shares at $70/$85/$100 thresholds (vs prior cycle's higher hurdles) while public shareholders absorbed a 98% dividend cut and 64% drawdown. Not dispositive on its own, but contributes to a coherent 'insider-favorable allocation under distress' pattern.

Remaining cash inflow from TMUSA is capped at the residual ~$192M against ongoing Cogent Fiber net losses exceeding $260M/yr. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Cogent Fiber acquisition has not produced wavelength-services revenue growth at anywhere near the scale needed to absorb the cost base. Service revenue of $54M against operating expenses of $258M means the business is losing $0.79 of operating profit per $1.00 of revenue, and the T-Mobile subsidy is finite. The 10-K's narrative emphasis on '1,068 wave-enabled locations' is a quantity claim that has not converted to material revenue. Wavelength is the consensus growth story; the actual financial trajectory contradicts it. With T-Mobile subsidy ~$192M remaining and current losses ~$260M/yr, the gap closes within ~8-9 quarters absent a major step-up in wavelength bookings.

summary: CCOI presents a concentrated R/f/M short profile centered on (1) a 98% dividend cut announced Q4 2025 (frozen at $0.02/qtr in 2026 by 2/18/26 Board action) after 13 years of dividend growth, (2) a CEO MARGIN-LOAN FORCED LIQUIDATION of 2,659,578 shares ($82.5M) on Aug 7-8 2025 — Form 4 footnotes explicitly state 'non-volitional transfer to lender' at 7-9% market discounts, (3) ZERO open-market code-P purchases by any C-suite officer or director in the entire 2025-2026 drawdown despite a -64.6% drawdown, (4) a $750M 2027 unsecured-note maturity wall against $148.5M unrestricted cash and NEGATIVE FY2025 operating cash flow, (5) Cogent Fiber Business losing $260M+/yr against $54M of wavelength revenue with the finite $700M T-Mobile IP-Transit subsidy mostly exhausted, and (6) repeated CEO performance-share forfeitures (cash-flow tranches forfeited in 2024 AND 2025) followed by a Feb-2026 re-grant lowering price-target hurdles. Counter-signals: clean Ernst & Young auditor opinion with no going-concern qualification, $105.8M buyback authorization remaining. Verdict: SHORT-tier — the disclosure-trust deficit is concentrated in the canonical Form-4 Mode-B finding (the CEO margin call is the cleanest 'opposite of management's confidence framing' signal possible) and the combination of dividend collapse + 2027 refinancing wall + zero insider buying is the dominant Signal OS pattern.
